prerequisites: Calculus: continuity, differentiability and integrability for functions of one real variable.
Basic knowledge of the linear functions in finite dimension vector space.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge in differential calculus for functions of several real variables, on sequences and series of functions and on ordinary differential equations.
Develop analysis and problem solving skills which are essential in most of the jobs, especially for engineers.
Acquire basic knowledge on sequences and series of functions, on differential equations and on differential calculus for functions of multiple real variables.
Develop the ability to solve mathematical problems using the techniques of mathematical analysis.
Be able to independently study topics related to those in the syllabus.
Communicate with mathematical language on the course topics.

syllabus_topics: First order differential equations in normal form and notion of solution.
First order linear equations and associated Cauchy problem: existence, uniqueness.
Local and global existence and uniqueness theorem.
Application to a Cauchy problem associated with Bernoulli-type equations.
Linear equations of order k with variable coefficients.
General solution of a non-homogeneous equation.
Equations with constant coefficients and characteristic polynomial.
Particular solution of an equation with a quasi-trigonometric forcing term.
Directional derivative, partial derivatives, gradient, proof of Fermat's theorem, Schwarz's theorem, study of the image of a continuous function on a compact connected set.
Differential and gradient, and their geometric interpretation.
Chain rule, characterization of functions with zero gradient, Hessian matrix.
Classification theorem of points with zero gradient using the Hessian matrix.

Kinematic interpretation of curves, tangent vector as velocity, Jacobian matrix, tangent space, unit vector normal to the graph, equation of the plane tangent to the graph at a point of a C^1 function.
Uniform convergence vs. integrals and derivatives.
Series of functions and their convergence.
Point-wise and uniform convergence of the Fourier series.
Proof of the global existence and uniqueness theorem for first-order differential equations in normal form.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. Passing the written test is essential to access the oral test. The written test comprises three problems, reflecting the main parts of the syllabus. The oral exam focuses on a deep-dive topic chosen by the candidate, plus additional questions on the syllabus and the written test.
